title_en: Guan Hua — false declaration of registered capital

full_text_en:
Guan Hua — Crime of Falsely Declaring Registered Capital

Procuratorial Authority: People's Procuratorate of Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Defendant: Guan Hua, male, 28 years old, former manager of Urumqi Huarong Pawnshop, arrested on August 6, 1997.

Defense Counsel: Duan Zhigang, Wang Hong, lawyers from Xinjiang Saide Law Firm.

The People's Procuratorate of Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, filed a public prosecution with the Intermediate People's Court of Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, against the defendant Guan Hua for the crime of falsely declaring registered capital.

Prosecutor's Charges: The defendant Guan Hua fabricated false supporting documents, used false credit certificates, and fraudulently obtained the business license of Urumqi Renli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Renli Company). Guan Hua's conduct violated the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of falsely declaring registered capital. A conviction and punishment are requested according to law.

The defendant Guan Hua argued: I did not fabricate any supporting documents.

Guan Hua's defense counsel contended: Guan Hua lacked the subjective intent to falsely declare registered capital or to fraudulently obtain business registration. In fact, after the company was established, he made up for the company's capital, as confirmed by deposit slips in the case file. Moreover, Guan Hua's conduct did not cause serious consequences and did not involve any other crimes. Therefore, it was merely an ordinary administrative violation and did not constitute the crime of falsely declaring registered capital as provided in the Criminal Law.

The Intermediate People's Court of Urumqi City found after trial:

The defendant Guan Hua was originally an employee of the International Business Department of the Agricultural Bank of China, Xinjiang Branch. Guan decided to establish a company in order to join the Urumqi pawnbroking industry under the company's name. In January 1996, Guan Hua instructed Yu Xiaojiang, an unemployed person, to fill out an application form for establishing Renli Company. Subsequently, Guan Hua, without informing his mother-in-law Hu Juanfen, used her identity card and photograph to fabricate a written application stating that Hu Juanfen would invest RMB 580,000 in Renli Company. He also took advantage of his business relationship with Ma Zhimao, manager of Xinjiang Haihua Property Management Company, and without Ma Zhimao's knowledge, used Ma's identity card, photograph, and company seal to fabricate a written application stating that Ma Zhimao would invest RMB 400,000 in Renli Company. To obtain a credit certificate, Guan Hua also fabricated a printed document stating: "Urumqi Renli Industrial Development Co., Ltd. is one of our bank's clients and has opened an account with our bank. The company's deposit balance as of January 24, 1996, is RMB 1 million." He approached Ma Wenxue, then president of the Development Zone Sub-branch of the Urumqi Corps Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Development Zone Sub-branch), and requested that Ma affix the bank's seal to the document. Ma Wenxue, for the purpose of "attracting clients and deposits" for his sub-branch, affixed the seal of the Development Zone Sub-branch to the false credit certificate fabricated by Guan Hua. Guan Hua then took this false credit certificate to Xinjiang Yingte Audit Firm and requested capital verification. Seeing that Guan Hua held a credit certificate issued by a financial institution, the audit firm issued a so-called capital verification certificate stating that "Renli Company has capital of RMB 1 million, of which Hu Juanfen invested RMB 580,000, Ma Zhimao invested RMB 400,000, and Yu Xiaojiang invested RMB 20,000," without actually conducting a capital verification. Guan Hua also fabricated a false lease agreement for premises to prove that Renli Company had a business location. On January 29, 1996, relying on this series of false documents and without any actual capital contribution, Guan Hua applied to the Urumqi Administration for Industry and Commerce to establish Renli Company. The Administration, believing that the written documents provided by Guan Hua met the conditions for company registration, issued a business license for Renli Company, with the approved business scope being "hardware and electrical appliances." Guan Hua subsequently opened three bank accounts in the name of Renli Company.

After Renli Company was established, it did not conduct any business activities related to "hardware and electrical appliances." In June 1996, Renli Company, together with Xinjiang Jinsui Property Management Co., Ltd. and three other companies, each investing RMB 250,000, established Urumqi Huarong Pawnshop, with the defendant Guan Hua serving as chairman of the board. Shortly after opening, the People's Bank of China notified that the registered capital of the pawnshop must reach the state-mandated amount of RMB 5 million to continue operations. To make the pawnshop's book capital appear to meet the RMB 5 million registered capital requirement, Guan Hua used Renli Company's three accounts for "funds shuffling" and cash withdrawals. In August 1996, Guan Hua, through personal connections, obtained three official checks from Yin Weian, president of the Urumqi Corps Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China, in the amounts of RMB 2 million, RMB 22,654.67, and RMB 424,763.20, respectively, and deposited them into Renli Company's account. He then immediately transferred RMB 250,000 to Huarong Pawnshop's account as Renli Company's capital contribution for capital increase. In September 1996, Guan Hua withdrew cash from Renli Company and transferred funds to the pawnshop three times, totaling RMB 900,000, as capital contributions for the capital increase of the pawnshop's other shareholders. Over the period of one year and seven months following the establishment of Renli Company, Guan Hua used the three accounts opened by Renli Company to conduct "funds shuffling" and cash withdrawals totaling RMB 12,152,000.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence:

1. The false credit certificate with the seal of the Development Zone Sub-branch affixed;
2. The testimony of witness Ma Wenxue, confirming that, under circumstances where Renli Company had neither opened an account nor had any funds, he violated regulations to issue a false certificate for Guan Hua;
3. A certificate from the Development Zone Sub-branch, confirming that the content of the credit certificate it issued to Renli Company on January 24, 1996, was erroneous;
4. The business license of Renli Company, showing its registered capital as RMB 1 million;
5. The confession of the defendant Guan Hua, stating that he completed all matters related to the company's establishment on his own without having any funds himself or receiving any capital contributions from others.

The Intermediate People's Court of Urumqi City held:

A company is one of the basic entities in a market economy and plays an important role in market economic activities. To enhance the transparency and security of companies, China has established a company registration system, with registered capital being one of the main elements of company registration. As a part of a company's operating capital, registered capital is a fundamental guarantee for a company to bear risks and repay debts. If the amount of falsely declared registered capital is huge, it not only violates the company registration system but also poses a significant threat to the security of capital and debts, causing substantial losses to society. Therefore, Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes against the Company Law, adopted on February 28, 1995, and Article 158 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (1997 revision) both stipulate that the act of falsely declaring registered capital in a huge amount and with serious consequences constitutes a crime.

The defendant Guan Hua used a false credit certificate to falsely declare registered capital of RMB 1 million, fraudulently obtained company registration, and the amount of falsely declared registered capital was huge. After fraudulently obtaining company registration, Guan Hua not only failed to conduct business activities within the approved scope but also used the company's accounts for "funds shuffling," facilitating the injection of false capital into other companies, thereby undermining the state's supervision and management of industrial, commercial, and financial activities, with serious consequences. Guan Hua's conduct has violated Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes against the Company Law and constitutes the crime of falsely declaring registered capital. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Criminal Law, he shall be punished in accordance with Article 158 of the Criminal Law.

Defense counsel for the defendant Guan Hua argued that after Renli Company was established, the funds in its bank accounts exceeded RMB 1 million, contending that Guan Hua lacked subjective criminal intent and had objectively made up for the registered capital, and therefore his conduct did not constitute a crime. Upon investigation, although the funds in Renli Company's accounts exceeded RMB 1 million after its establishment, these funds were merely working capital used by Renli Company for "funds shuffling" and cash withdrawals. They could not prove that Guan Hua had subsequently invested these funds as registered capital, much less that Guan Hua possessed these funds at the time of applying for company registration. Therefore, the defense argument was not accepted. Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Urumqi City rendered the following judgment on November 15, 1999:

The defendant Guan Hua is convicted of the crime of falsely declaring registered capital and is sentenced to a fine of RMB 20,000.

After the judgment of first instance, Guan Hua appealed, raising the defense arguments presented by his defense counsel at trial as grounds for appeal.

The High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region found upon trial: The appellant Guan Hua used false credit certificates and other supporting documents to falsely declare registered capital of RMB 1 million, fraudulently obtained company registration, and the amount of falsely declared registered capital was huge with serious consequences. His conduct constituted the crime of falsely declaring registered capital and shall be punished according to law. Guan Hua's grounds for appeal are untenable and shall be rejected. The facts found by the first-instance judgment are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, the conviction is accurate, the sentence is appropriate, and the trial procedure is lawful, and the judgment shall be affirmed. Accordingly, the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered the following ruling on December 13, 1999:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.
